---
title: "Workshop"
subtitle: "One session file gives an HTML page, a PDF handout and a deck."
description: "The workshop type of the mcanouil extension: session metadata, the workshop blocks, exercises and solutions in each format, and the references to solutions."
---

A workshop session is one `.qmd` file that renders to three formats.
For a website around the sessions, use an [atelier](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-atelier) project.

```yaml
title: "Authoring essentials"
date: 2026-11-13
lang: en-GB
format:
  mcanouil-html: default
  mcanouil-typst: default
  mcanouil-revealjs: default
extensions:
  mcanouil:
    type: workshop
    event: "Mastering Quarto CLI"
    session:
      number: 2
      total: 7
    duration: "90 min"
    solutions: end
```

- The kicker shows "Session 2 of 7".
- The duration shows beside the date.
- The footer shows the event, "Session 2" and the page or slide number.

## Blocks

| Class | Label |
| --- | --- |
| `.objectives` | Objectives |
| `.prerequisites` | Prerequisites |
| `.exercise` | Exercise 2.1 · 15 min · pairs |
| `.solution` | Solution |
| `.checkpoint` | Checkpoint |

: The workshop blocks and their labels. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

Each block has a visible label from the language files, so it does not rely on colour.
An exercise is numbered with the session number and its position.
Without a session, the number is its position only.
The `duration` and `format` attributes of an exercise add to its label.

```markdown
::: {.exercise duration="15 min" format="pairs"}

Create `portfolio.qmd`, a document that renders to HTML and to Typst.

::: {.solution}

Set two formats in the front matter.

:::

:::
```

A `.solution` must be inside an `.exercise`.
Outside an exercise, the render stops with a message.

## Solutions in each format

| Format | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| HTML | A closed `<details>` disclosure. |
| Reveal.js | A block of the veil group `solutions`, hidden until the presenter shows it. |
| PDF, `solutions: end` | A "Solution: page n" link in the exercise, and the solutions on the last pages. |
| PDF, `solutions: inline` | The solution in its exercise. |
| PDF, `solutions: hide` | No solutions. |

: How each format shows a solution. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

The solution fades in only when the reader has no reduced motion setting.

## Solution names

A `name` attribute adds to the label: "Solution · Worked answer".

```markdown
::: {.solution name="Worked answer"}
```

If a solution has no `name` and starts with a heading, that heading becomes the name.
It then shows in the label and not as a heading.
This is the behaviour of Quarto for proofs.

## References to solutions

Give a solution an identifier with the `sol-` prefix, then cite it.

```markdown
::: {.solution #sol-a}

The answer.

:::

Compare with @sol-a.
```

- `@sol-a` reads "Solution 2.2" and links to the solution.
- `[@sol-b; @sol-a]` reads "Solution 2.2, Solution 2.1".
- With `solutions: hide`, the reference is text with no link.

Cite solutions in a citation of their own.
If a citation mixes solutions and other references, the render gives a warning and Quarto cannot resolve the solutions.

::: {.callout-warning}

Do not use a hyphen in a solution identifier other than the `sol-` prefix, for example `#worked-answer`.
Quarto stops on such an identifier before the extension runs ([quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15113](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/15113)).
Use `#sol-worked` or `#workedanswer` until this is fixed.

:::

## `.solution` outside workshops

Quarto uses `.solution` for its own proof environment.
In a document that is not a workshop, a `.solution` div stays a Quarto proof.

## Code

Code ligatures are off for all code, in every format and every type.
`->`, `!=` and `<=` keep their characters, which is important for teaching syntax.

## Handout headings

The first heading of the PDF handout must be level 1, because the PDF/UA-1 standard does not accept a skipped level.
Start each session with a `#` heading.
